text:
maria: Quick sanity-check doc for the control-trial we ran yesterday — putting notes here so infra + ML have a single source.
ash: thanks, saw some weird noise on the 1k token tail. do we have the exact config used?
maria: pasted below, this was the exact bench harness used for all models to keep it fair (same prompts, decoding params, stop seqs, tokenizer flags).
default config:
```json
{
  "batch_size": 8,
  "concurrency": 16,
  "max_tokens": 1024,
  "decode": { "temp": 0.0, "top_p": 0.95, "max_new_tokens": 256 },
  "stop_sequences": ["\n"],
  "tokenizer_utf8_align": true
}
```
ash: the important bit is tokenizer_utf8_align = true, that ensured identical tokenization across our tokenizers shim. without it we saw off-by-one decode diffs.
devon: what about KV cache warm vs cold? our runtime has special warm-path kernel selection. were those toggled?
maria: yes — we ran three passes: cold (no cache), warm (single prefix cached per model), and +batching probe. kernel selection allowed to auto-pick based on seq_len.
sam: kernel selector logs looked clean but I noticed fallback to generic-cuda on a couple of runs. timestamped logs: `selector: model-x -> opt-kv-fused` then later `selector: model-x -> generic` around run 13.
qi: that fallback maps to a perf regression on GPU due to a missing matmul-opt kernel for seqlen 512. i'm working on a repro.
bench-bot: perf run 1748881234: model-a vs model-b vs model-c — 4800 requests, tails removed, p50/p95/p99 collected. artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/control-trial/1748881234/
ash: can we avoid p99 fusion noise by dropping runs where concurrency > 16? some tail jitter correlated with background infra autoscaling.
infra-bot: note: there was a node restart in us-west-2 at 1748881260; small number of in-flight requests re-routed.
maria: added that note — runs 7 and 8 impacted, excluded from summary.
devon: what about batching heuristics? did we use dynamic batching window = 3ms or static grouping?
maria: dynamic window 3ms + size cap 16. we also tested an aggressive profile (1ms window) but it increased latency p95 by 8% for model-c.
qi: attaching profiler snippet that showed KV cache misses spiking in the aggressive case:
```
KV cache miss rate: baseline 0.3% -> aggressive 1.9%
Batch fill rate: baseline 78% -> aggressive 92%
Latency p95: baseline 120ms -> aggressive 130ms
```
sam: so more batching helped throughput but cost us tail latency due to repeat prefix eviction?
devon: yes, eviction + cold-start kernels for short sequences. for model-c, kernel selection cost outweighed batching gains at 1ms.
maria: conclusion bullets i propose to add to the run notes (open to edits):
- Use tokenizer alignment flag consistently across toolchain to prevent semantic token mismatches.
- Start with dynamic batching window = 3ms for mixed workload; only push to 1ms if strict throughput wins and tail latency is acceptable.
- Add kernel selector guard for seqlen=512 on model-c to avoid fallback regression (qi to follow up).
- Always record node-level infra events and mark runs impacted by restarts; correlate with p99.
- For apples-to-apples model comparisons: require identical sampling seeds / deterministic decode when comparing logits or exact text equality.
ash: +1. also add a small section on how we stitch replay harness prompts to match live temporal distribution (we sampled by session-length buckets).
qi: i'll raise a PR with the selector fix and add a small smoke test into the harness that fails the bench if selector falls back to generic kernel.
bench-bot: artifact summary uploaded: s3://redwood-bench/control-trial/1748881234/summary.json (contains per-run traces + kernel selection matrix) :rocket:
maria: thanks all — i'll fold these notes into the canonical doc and tag the perf dashboard. if anyone wants the raw logs ping me and i'll share a signed url. :thumbsup:
